summary.en: A **participle clause** shortens a longer sentence and makes your writing tighter. Use the **-ing form** for active meaning (_Walking home, I met an old friend_), the **-ed form** for passive meaning (_Built in 1900, the bridge is still in use_), and **having + past participle** for an action that happened first. The unstated subject of the participle must be the same as the subject of the main clause.
summary.es: Equivalen a oraciones de gerundio o participio españolas («Caminando a casa…», «Construido en 1900…»), pero el sujeto sobrentendido debe coincidir con el de la oración principal.

form: Active, at the same time: **-ing** (_Waiting for the bus, she read the news._)
Active, earlier action: **having + past participle** (_Having finished, he left._)
Passive: **-ed / being + past participle / having been + past participle** (_Seen from above, the city looks tiny._)
Reduced relative clause: _people living nearby_ (= who live nearby), _a book written by a friend_ (= which was written)
After time words: **before/after/while/when/since + -ing** (_After leaving school, he travelled._)
Negative: **not + participle** (_Not knowing the answer, I guessed._)

uses.text: **Two actions at the same time**: _She sat by the window, **watching** the rain._
**One action before another**: _**Having read** the instructions, I started the machine._
**Reason**: _**Not wanting** to be late, he took a taxi._
**Describing a noun (reduced relative clause)**: _The woman **sitting** next to me was a doctor._ _The documents **sent** yesterday are missing._
**Passive meaning**: _**Surprised** by the noise, the dog barked._

note.en: Make sure the subject of the participle is the same as the main subject, or the sentence becomes illogical (a dangling participle).
note.es: El sujeto del participio debe ser el de la oración principal; si no, la frase queda incoherente.

mistakes.wrong: Walking down the street, a car hit my bike.
mistakes.right: Walking down the street, I saw a car hit my bike.

why.en: The subject of walking must be the main subject (I), not a car.
why.es: Quien camina es «yo», así que el sujeto principal debe ser I.

mistakes.wrong: Finished the work, she went home.
mistakes.right: Having finished the work, she went home.

why.en: For an earlier active action, use having + past participle.
why.es: Para una acción anterior, having + participio.

mistakes.wrong: The boy sitting on his own was looked sad.
mistakes.right: The boy sitting on his own looked sad.

why.en: The participle replaces a relative clause. Don't add another verb for the same subject.
why.es: El participio sustituye a who was sitting; no repitas otro verbo auxiliar.

mistakes.wrong: Being tired, the bed was where I went.
mistakes.right: Being tired, I went to bed.

why.en: Keep the same subject in both parts of the sentence.
why.es: Ambas partes necesitan el mismo sujeto: Being tired, I…

examples.en: Feeling nervous, she checked her notes again.
examples.es: Sintiéndose nerviosa, volvió a revisar sus notas.

examples.en: Having missed the last train, we had to walk home.
examples.es: Como habíamos perdido el último tren, tuvimos que volver andando.

examples.en: Written in a hurry, the email contained several mistakes.
examples.es: Escrito con prisa, el correo tenía varios errores.

examples.en: The people waiting outside look frozen.
Not having a car, he cycles to work.
After talking to my manager, I felt much better.
The house, built by my grandfather, is now a museum.
Having been warned about the traffic, we left early.
Most of the students questioned said they liked the course.
Seen from the top, the valley looks like a green carpet.

practice.prompt: ___ the report, Maria sent it to her boss.

explanation.en: Finishing came before sending, so we use having + past participle.

practice.prompt: The photographs ___ at the exhibition were all taken in Peru.

explanation.en: The photographs are shown (passive), so use the -ed participle.

practice.prompt: ___ the answer, he asked the teacher for help.

explanation.en: Active meaning and the same subject (he): not + -ing.

practice.prompt: Opening the door, ___ the room was empty.

explanation.en: The person opening the door must be the subject of the main clause.
